public health dental program. In this report, we share an
overview of the Dental Program Components and how they work
together to support clients with oral health screening, followed by
help with Getting Any Needed dental treatment and connecting them with the appropriate funding
program. As you are aware, the Federal Canadian Dental Care
Plan, also called the CDCP, has rolled out in Canada.
Members of Council had expressed interest in receiving an update
on how this program has impacted the Dental Care Landscape
in our Community and Public Health's Dental Program. The Canadian
Plan has expanded coverage for many Canadians and has created
new pathways to essential dental care. Over the past year,
our Dental Staff have worked with local families to register
for the program when eligible. However, for many low -
income families, some remain ineligible and others, although eligible are
still unable to access care. In this report, you will
see examples of how low - income families still face
co - payments and balance billing. Other barriers to access
include treatment delays or challenges obtaining approval for more complex
care. Prior to the Canadian plan, the provincial healthy smiles
Ontario program supported eligible low-income families with access
to free dental care. While that program still exists, most
Community providers have chosen to move away from offering this
program as a standalone coverage option now that the Canadian
plan has come into effect. This has created additional pressure
for families who are only covered by the Healthy Smiles
Ontario Program, but cannot find a Community Provider to access
the care they need. The result is a more complicated
access environment for residents and for staff. Public Health Dental
Program staff are not simply providing direct clinical services. They
are assessing eligibility across multiple programs. Helping families navigate coverage
rules. Supporting transitions to Community Providers where appropriate and ensuring
that limited tax levy funded Dental Clinic Resources are
prioritized for residents who do not have access to other
options. This report situates the public health dental program within
a broader health system context, highlighting that while federal and
provincial programs are essential. They do not fully resolve local
access barriers and gaps remain for some of Waterloo Regions most vulnerable residents
often leaving the public health dental clinic as their only
option for care. Thank you. Okay, are there any questions.

Uh, we are pleased to introduce the 2025 Public Health
Infection Prevention and Control and Safe Water Inspections Report. This
report provides an update to Regional Council as our Board
of Health on Public Health's Inspection Programs for Infection Prevention
and Control, safe drinking water, and recreational water. These programs
are an important part of public health's mandate to protect
residents by reducing preventable risks in settings where people receive
services, gather, work, learn and play. They also reflect public
health's role as both regulator and partner supporting operators and
service providers to meet provincial requirements while taking enforcement action
when needed. In 2026, our teams continue to conduct inspections,
respond to complaints, and adverse events address emerging risks and
provide education and guidance across a growing and changing region.
This work included personal service settings, recreational water facilities, and
small drinking water systems. Demand for these programs continues to
increase. The number of premises requiring inspection is growing, including
more diverse and novel facilities and services. Public health is
also responding to a growing number of service requests, including
complaints. Using a risk-based approach public health prioritizes
inspections, monitoring, education, and regulatory activities were the potential for
illness or injury as greatest. So in closing, this report
provides council with an overview of the local public health
protection activities that support the reduction of infectious disease transmission,
waterborne illness, and injury across the community, and

Um, this funding, as tends to typically be the case,
uh, these days has been awarded from CMHC to the
housing provider in the form of a forgivable loan. And
that loan gets registered on the title, uh, of the
property in the form of an encumbrance. And what that
does is it ensures that the conditions of the loan
are going to be met for the term of the
agreement. So the funding provided is 5 million dollars. The
term of the agreement, uh, is for 10 years. And
the conditions being that the units that they provide and
that are repaired remain affordable, um, for that period of
time. At the end of that period of time, 10
years in this case, the loan is then forgiven. So
rather than providing a straight grant, uh, this is funding
that is provided in this format of a forgivable loan
that gets registered on title. And the issue then that
we're bringing forward, uh, is that our policy locally created
policy only permits a provider to encumber a property at
90 percent of its value by receiving this 5 million
dollar forgivable loan. They're exceeding that 90 percent threshold and
it goes up to about 116 percent. Staff are recommending that we make
an exception to our policy, um, in this case. Um,
there are a number of reasons supporting that. About 50
percent of the value, uh, that's encumbered on the property
right now is made up of these types of forgivable
loans. Um, so they're not, uh, loans like a mortgage
that you would typically understand. Um, this is a provider
that is in good standing, both financially and operationally, um,
with us as the service system manager. They are registered
not for profit with a long history. Um, and we
have no concerns about them continuing to provide, um, affordable
housing overall. And I think last reason of substance is
that CMHC's own policy allows a provider to encumber the
value of a property up to 120 percent as well. Um, for these
reasons, we see this exception as a, as a low
risk, uh, in this instance. And it will provide much
needed repair and retrofit funding to the provider, ensuring ongoing
sustainability of that property and upgrading the building and the
conditions that the tenants are living in. And beyond that,
recommendation staff are also, uh, in the next step section,
